 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The All-American 2026 WTA Finals Group 1 match between Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula lasted two hours and 39 minutes on Sunday in Indian Wells. Gauff won the match in three sets, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-2.
 During the match, Gauff excelled in covering the court, making it physically exhausting for Pegula to keep up with the two-time Grand Slam champion. In the post-match conference, Pegula said Gauff's movement made it difficult for her. This was also why Pegula looked pretty exhausted in the third set.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "It's tough when a match gets really physical against Coco; to be honest, it's probably not in my favor," Pegula told reporters as seen in Christian Court's X. "I think the first two sets especially were super physical, and I just had a little lull at the beginning of the third, which was unfortunate, like that first game… I thought her movement, I mean, I say this every time, but is the best on tour. Like, it's insane, her court coverage. I felt like I was coming into the net, sticking volleys, and I'm like ready to walk, turn around, and she's, even if I won the point, she was still there."
 Pegula also acknowledged the mistakes she made in the first set, including missed "volleys, overheads and short balls." Pegula had a break opportunity in the ninth game of the opening set, but she failed to execute. In the end, Gauff held her serve and went on to break the fellow American in the very next game to win the first set.
 Pegula and Gauff's match was one of two opening-day matches in Indian Wells on Sunday. The other match saw Linda Noskova beating Elena Rybakina's replacement, Marta Kostyuk, in straight sets.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Coco Gauff Gets Honest About Her Shoes' Condition After Jessica Pegula Encounter
 As Jessica Pegula explained, Gauff ran aggressively on the court, using her movement to gain a competitive advantage. Gauff herself acknowledged how much running the match required. She joked that her shoes were badly worn out, with pieces of rubber left on the court.
 "But I also had to run a lot," Gauff said. "My shoes are pretty torn up now. Some of my shoes… like somewhere on the court there. So I'm gonna have to change shoes tomorrow."
 Gauff also praised Pegula's ball striking.
 "Jess is an incredible player. We always go back and forth," Gauff said of Pegula via Yahoo Sports. "She does really great ball striking; she keeps the ball low when she's really aggressive. So I think today the key was just trying to be aggressive."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Gauff, who is seeking to win her second WTA Finals title, will face Linda Noskova in her next game. Meanwhile, Pegula will face Kostyuk in the other Group 1 match.
